what: The score combines insertion distance with the best single 2-opt gain involving either newly created edge, a radial savings term, route-versus-unassigned cluster affinity, capacity-gap quality, and a reward for a nearby customer that remains feasible afterward. It uses only the supplied distance matrix and runs in O(len(route) + len(unassigned)) time per evaluated insertion, with O(len(route)) temporary memory.
why: The radial term counteracts ordinary cheapest insertion's tendency to consume depot-near customers while leaving expensive peripheral customers for later routes. Affinity and feasible-continuation terms encourage compact geographic chains, while the capacity term helps avoid poorly usable residual capacity and accommodates heterogeneous demands such as near-capacity customers. The local 2-opt correction is tailored to the stated post-construction improvement phase and can recognize insertions whose apparent detour is immediately repairable. The coefficients are scale-aware but hand chosen; this is not a remaining-cost estimate, and the one-customer capacity lookahead and one-move 2-opt proxy cannot capture subset packing, later route interactions, or the full final local optimum.
